findings.finding: Fault classes are imbalanced: Container Hardware has 83 cases and Node Memory only 9 (ratio 9.2:1).

6 nodes have no trace features and 16 have no log features in any training sample (structural absence, not missing values); overall 81% of metric entries are exactly 0 (zero equals the series mean after ARMOR's scaling - inferred, so a zero is not a missing value).
11 channel pairs have |r| >= 0.95 on system-level training series (38 channels are constant and excluded); mean |r| within metrics is 0.15.

Root-cause-node deviation relative to other nodes (mean |value| ratio, training cases): metric 1.45 before vs 3.50 after injection; trace 0.90 before vs 1.82 after injection; log 1.05 before vs 1.69 after injection. Service-level cases average over all replicas of the named service.

37 channels are constant in the training partition. Heaviest tails: transport_closing_warning (3.3% of values beyond |3|), kpi_container_network_receive_MB (2.9% of values beyond |3|), duration (1.5% of values beyond |3|).

Under the proposed alternative split, 0 of 130 channels differ between training and validation by KS >= 0.2 (largest: kpi_container_memory_cache, KS 0.13). Exploratory: the split is pending approval and KS on pooled entries is sensitive to the zero mass.

Model-development statistics (scaler, structural masks, histograms, correlations, outliers, incident ratios on train cases) use only samples at or before the official AD boundary; temporal trends, descriptive stats and held-out-case rows are descriptive and labelled as such.
